steps.title: Prepare input images
steps.instruction: Resize each raw field image to the canonical resolution of 1184 × 864 pixels (or retain it if already at that size) and keep the original image for reference.

steps.title: Access generative reconstruction model
steps.instruction: Open the Gemini Nano Banana Pro image‑to‑image generation interface via its web‑based multimodal generation portal (accessed in January 2026). No low‑level diffusion parameters (sampler, denoising strength, random seed, CFG scale, number of diffusion steps, temperature) are exposed to the user.

steps.title: Set constraint‑based prompt
steps.instruction: Upload the prepared image as the sole visual reference and enter the fixed prompt: “Reconstruct the same target shrub/forage plant as an annotation‑ready image. Preserve the original plant identity, branching pattern, leaf distribution, flower and fruit structures, camera viewpoint, object scale, and canopy outline. Suppress the irrelevant background clutter like dry soil, litter, stones, and any visually confusing texture. Do not add new branches, leaves, flowers, stems, fruits, thorns, shadows, or plant parts. Do not remove visible plant organs. Do not stylize the image or generate artifacts. The output should remain a realistic RGB field‑image reconstruction suitable for vegetation segmentation and annotation.”

steps.title: Run reconstruction attempts
steps.instruction: For each image, perform up to three generation attempts using the same prompt and input image. If the first output satisfies all constraints, retain it; otherwise start a new session and regenerate with the identical prompt.

substeps.instruction: If rejected, start a new session.
If rejected, start a new session.

steps.title: Apply rejection criteria
steps.instruction: Discard any generated output that shows any of the following: altered canopy outline, hallucinated or removed branches/leaves/flowers/fruits/thorns, changed camera viewpoint or object scale, background replacement that intrudes into the target vegetation, stylized/cartoon‑like appearance, over‑smoothing, or any unrealistic artifact.

steps.title: Select optimal reconstruction
steps.instruction: From the accepted outputs, retain the image that provides the strongest background simplification while preserving the original shrub boundary, internal branching structure, and all visible plant organs. Preference is given to the reconstruction with the clearest vegetation‑background separation and unchanged biological form.

steps.title: Save final reconstructed image
steps.instruction: Save the selected reconstruction at the same 1184 × 864 pixel resolution to maintain spatial consistency with the original image and downstream products.

steps.title: Apply deterministic post‑processing
steps.instruction: Run the reported deterministic segmentation and refinement parameters (as listed in Table 1 of the original study) on the saved reconstruction to produce the final annotation‑ready vegetation prior.
